To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the impact of SSM on the optical signals transmitted over the proposed ultra-dense mixed-FOTS is negligible and that the most robust optical signal in the chosen transmission mode is NRZ-DPSQ modulated signal.

the SPM-induced distortions are more pronounced in case of 2-POLK signals and that the use of “non ITU” frequency intervals for WDM channels separation is beneficial for the system performance in terms of the SPM-induced signal degradation.
the impact of the SPM on the transmission performance is dependent on the used modulation format and that 2-Polsk signals are more susceptible than NRZ-DPS.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the investigation of the SPM induced distortions and the influence of these distortions on the performance of ultra-dense WDM transmission systems.
the investigation of the influence of SPM induced signal distortions on ultra-dense mixed WDM system.
the evaluation of the impact of SSM on the performance of ultra-dense WDM system with mixed bitrates and modulation formats.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the SPM induced signal distortions in chosen ultra-dense mixed WDM system are strongly dependent on used optical signal modulation format and the channel spacing.

SPM induced distortions in the chosen ultra-dense mixed WDM system can be mitigated by using appropriate optical signal modulation formats and/or by applying appropriate optical signal processing techniques.
the SPM-induced signal distortion can be reduced in such system configuration by using of NRZ-DPSQ signals and by increasing of the frequency channel separation.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

SPM-induced signal distortions are not negligible in such ultra-densely packed WDM transmission systems and that they should be taken into consideration in order to achieve a better understanding of their impact and to improve the performance of such transmission systems.
SPM is the most critical impairment in the proposed ultra-dense mixed optical transmission system.
the use of 2-POLKS modulation format in such ultra-densly WDM transmission systems should be carefully considered due to its high sensitivity to SPM induced distortions.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the SPM-induced signal distortion can be effectively suppressed by using optical filtering of the transmitted signals.
the use of ultra-dense WDM transmission mode is not a viable solution for the future high-speed FOTS.
the use of 2-POLKS signals in ultra-dense WDM transmission systems is not recommended due to the impact of the nonlinear effects.
